source_refs.note: Book p. 241-242: 13.3.1 Notation of Derivative, equations (iv)-(vi), dy/dx = f'(x), Note box, notation table (Leibniz, Newton, Lagrange, Euler), alternative form (vii), f'(a) as gradient at x = a

blocks.text:
Bachon, is sabaq ka maqsad yeh hai ke derivative ko likhne ke tamam tareeqe (notations) pehchan lein aur samajh lein ke yeh sab ek hi cheez ke naam hain. Bilkul aise jaise ek hi shakhs ko ghar mein ek naam se aur school mein doosre naam se bulaya jaye, insaan wohi rehta hai. Kitab kehti hai: derivative ke liye kai notations istemal hote hain. Ab tak humne \(f'(x)\) likha, jo \(f\) ka derivative hai \(x\) par. Ab function \(y = f(x)\) ke liye:
\[y + \delta y = f(x + \delta x) \quad \text{...(iv)}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Equation (iv) keh kya rahi hai? Jab \(x\) mein thori si tabdeeli \(\delta x\) ("delta x") aati hai, to \(y\) bhi thora sa badalta hai; is tabdeeli ko \(\delta y\) kehte hain. Naya input \(x + \delta x\) hai, to naya output \(f(x + \delta x)\) hai. Aur naya output kya hai? Purana \(y\) jama us ki tabdeeli \(\delta y\).
Ek chhota qadam jo kitab chhor deti hai: (iv) ki dono sides se \(y = f(x)\) minus karein, to sirf tabdeeli bachti hai:
\[\delta y = f(x+\delta x) - f(x)\]
Kyun: humein \(y\) ki tabdeeli chahiye, poori nayi value nahin. Agli line mein isi equation ko \(\delta x\) se divide kiya jata hai.

Ab dono sides ko \(\delta x\) se divide karte hain:
\[\dfrac{\delta y}{\delta x} = \dfrac{f(x+\delta x)-f(x)}{\delta x}\]
\[\text{...(v)}\]
Yeh fraction kya hai? \(y\) ki tabdeeli taqseem \(x\) ki tabdeeli, yani average rate of change (ausat raftaar-e-tabdeeli). Ab (v) ki dono sides ki limit lete hain jab \(\delta x \to 0\):
\[\lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{\delta y}{\delta x}\]
\[= \lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{f(x+\delta x)-f(x)}{\delta x}\]
\[\text{...(vi)}\]

Limit lene se average rate "is lamhe" ka rate ban jata hai. \(\lim\limits_{\delta x \to 0}\frac{\delta y}{\delta x}\) ko ek naya chhota sa naam diya jata hai: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\). To (vi) ko yun likhte hain:
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = f'(x)\]

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Numbers ke saath dekhte hain ke \(\frac{\delta y}{\delta x}\) kaise \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ki taraf jata hai. Function \(y = x^{2}\) lein aur \(x = 3\) se shuru karein (\(y = 9\)).
Agar \(\delta x = 0.1\): naya \(y = (3.1)^{2} = 9.61\), to \(\delta y = 0.61\) aur \(\frac{\delta y}{\delta x} = 6.1\).
Agar \(\delta x = 0.01\): naya \(y = (3.01)^{2} = 9.0601\), to \(\delta y = 0.0601\) aur \(\frac{\delta y}{\delta x} = 6.01\).
Dekha? Jitna \(\delta x\) chhota karte jayen, ratio \(6\) ke qareeb aata jata hai. Yahi \(6\) us point par \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) hai. Ghor karein: \(\delta y\) aur \(\delta x\) dono zero ki taraf ja rahe hain, lekin un ka ratio zero nahin, \(6\) ki taraf ja raha hai. Isi liye \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ko "\(dy\) taqseem \(dx\)" nahin samajhte; yeh ratio ki limit hai.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Kitab ka note: symbol \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) \(y\) ke derivative ke liye istemal hota hai \(x\) ke lihaz se (with respect to \(x\)), aur yahan yeh \(dy\) aur \(dx\) ka quotient (taqseem) nahin hai. \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ko \(y'\) bhi likhte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
In symbols ko parhna seekhiye:
\(\frac{\delta y}{\delta x}\): "delta y by delta x". Yeh asal fraction hai: \(y\) ki tabdeeli taqseem \(x\) ki tabdeeli.
\(\frac{dy}{dx}\): "dee y by dee x". Yeh us fraction ki limit hai. Yeh ek hi symbol hai, jaise "Rs." ek nishaan hai, do alag cheezen nahin. Is mein \(d\) ko cancel nahin kar sakte, aur akela \(dy\) yahan koi maani nahin rakhta.
\(\frac{d}{dx}\) akela ek hukm (instruction) hai: "\(x\) ke lihaz se derivative lo". Jaise \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^{2})\) ka matlab hai "\(x^{2}\) ka derivative nikalo".

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text: Bohat se students \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) dekh kar \(d\) ko upar neeche se kaat dete hain aur \(\frac{y}{x}\) likh dete hain. Yeh bilkul ghalat hai. Misal: \(y = x^{2}\) ho to \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x\) hai (yeh Example 3 mein saabit hoga), jab ke \(\frac{y}{x} = x\) hai. Dono alag hain.

Ab kitab ek table deti hai jis mein mukhtalif mathematicians ke derivative ke notations hain (\(y = f(x)\) ke liye). Hum ne Newton wala khana sahi shakal mein likha hai; ghalti ki tafseel neeche box mein hai.

blocks.caption: Mukhtalif mathematicians ke derivative ke notations (y = f(x) ke liye)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab Newton ka notation \(f^{\bullet}(x)\) ya \(y^{\bullet}\) chhaapti hai, yani dot ko harf ke saath oopar power ki tarah rakh deti hai. Newton ke notation mein dot harf ke bilkul oopar hota hai: \(\dot{f}(x)\) ya \(\dot{y}\) (parhte hain "f dot", "y dot"). Newton zyada tar waqt (time) ke lihaz se tabdeeli ke liye yeh nishaan lagate the; Physics mein \(\dot{s}\) velocity hoti hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Charon notations bilkul ek hi cheez batate hain: \(y = f(x)\) ka derivative. Is kitab mein aap zyada tar do dekhenge: Leibniz ka \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) aur Lagrange ka \(f'(x)\) (parhte hain "f dash x" ya "f prime x").
Har ek ka fayda: Leibniz wala saaf batata hai ke kis variable ke lihaz se derivative liya (neeche \(dx\)), is liye aage chain rule mein bohat kaam aata hai. Lagrange wala chhota hai, jaldi likha jata hai. Euler ka \(D\) ek operator (amal karne wala nishaan) hai: \(Df\) ka matlab "\(f\) ka derivative lo". Newton wala Physics mein waqt ke saath tabdeeli ke liye aam hai.
The derivative at a point x = a

Ab kitab definition ki ek doosri shakal deti hai jo kisi ek khaas point par kaam aati hai. Agar \(x + \delta x\) ki jagah \(x\) likhein aur \(x\) ki jagah \(a\), to \(f(x + \delta x) - f(x)\) ban jata hai \(f(x) - f(a)\), aur independent variable (azad variable) mein tabdeeli \(\delta x\) ab \(x - a\) ban jati hai.
Is liye fraction \(\frac{f(x+\delta x)-f(x)}{\delta x}\) ab yun likha jata hai:
\[\dfrac{f(x)-f(a)}{x-a} \quad \text{...(vii)}\]
Jab \(x \to a\) ho to (vii) ki limit:
\[\lim_{x \to a}\dfrac{f(x)-f(a)}{x-a} = f'(a)\]
Yahan \(f'(a)\) ko \(f\) ka derivative ya gradient (dhalwan) \(x = a\) par kehte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh wahi definition kyun hai? Pehli shakal mein fixed point \(x\) hai aur chalne wala point \(x + \delta x\). Doosri shakal mein fixed point \(a\) hai aur chalne wala point \(x\). Dono mein oopar "function ki tabdeeli" hai aur neeche "input ki tabdeeli". Input ki tabdeeli ek mein \(\delta x\) hai, doosre mein \(x - a\). Aur "\(\delta x \to 0\)" aur "\(x \to a\)" ek hi baat hai: chalne wala point fixed point ke qareeb se qareeb tar aa raha hai.
Graph par dekhein to \(\frac{f(x)-f(a)}{x-a}\) secant line (do points \((a, f(a))\) aur \((x, f(x))\) ko milane wali line) ka slope hai. Jab \(x\), \(a\) ke qareeb aata hai to secant ghoom kar tangent ban jati hai, aur slope tangent ka gradient ban jata hai. Yahi baat aap ne 13.1 mein dekhi thi.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Doosri shakal se \(f(x) = x^{2}\) ka gradient \(x = 3\) par nikalte hain (yeh kitab mein nahin):
\[\dfrac{f(x)-f(3)}{x-3} = \dfrac{x^{2}-9}{x-3}\]
\[= \dfrac{(x-3)(x+3)}{x-3} = x + 3,\ (x \ne 3)\]
\[f'(3) = \lim_{x \to 3}(x+3) = 6\]
Kyun: \(x^{2} - 9\) difference of squares hai, is liye \((x-3)(x+3)\) mein toot jata hai. \(x \ne 3\) hai, is liye \((x-3)\) cancel karna jaaiz hai. Phir \(x = 3\) rakhna mehfooz hai kyun ke ab neeche zero nahin.
Tasdeeq: Example 3(b) mein hum \(f'(x) = 2x\) nikalenge; \(x = 3\) par \(2(3) = 6\). Jawab mil gaya.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(f(x) = 5x\) ka derivative \(x = 2\) par doosri shakal se nikaliye.
Jawab: \(\frac{5x - 10}{x - 2} = \frac{5(x-2)}{x-2} = 5\), to \(f'(2) = 5\). Samajh mein bhi aata hai: \(y = 5x\) seedhi line hai jis ka slope har jagah \(5\) hai.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Agar sawal \(f'(x)\) ya \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) aam taur par maange to pehli shakal \(\lim\limits_{\delta x \to 0}\frac{f(x+\delta x)-f(x)}{\delta x}\) istemal karein. Agar koi khaas point \(x = a\) diya ho to doosri shakal \(\lim\limits_{x \to a}\frac{f(x)-f(a)}{x-a}\) aksar jaldi kaam karti hai. Working sahi ho to dono par poore number milte hain. Har line mein "\(\lim\)" likhna na bhooliye jab tak limit asal mein le na li jaye.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(y + \delta y = f(x+\delta x)\), is liye \(\delta y = f(x+\delta x) - f(x)\).
2. \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \lim\limits_{\delta x \to 0}\frac{\delta y}{\delta x} = f'(x)\): average rate ki limit hi derivative hai.
3. \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ek symbol hai, fraction nahin; isay \(y'\) bhi likhte hain.
4. Notations: Leibniz \(\frac{dy}{dx}\), \(\frac{df}{dx}\); Newton \(\dot{y}\); Lagrange \(f'(x)\); Euler \(Df(x)\). Sab ka matlab ek.
5. \(f'(a) = \lim\limits_{x \to a}\frac{f(x)-f(a)}{x-a}\): yeh \(x = a\) par derivative (gradient) hai, yani ek number.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) mein \(d\) cancel kar ke \(\frac{y}{x}\) likh dena. Yeh fraction nahin, ek nishaan hai.
2. \(\delta x\) ko \(\delta \times x\) samajhna. Yeh ek hi miqdaar hai: \(x\) mein tabdeeli.
3. \(f'(x)\) aur \(f'(a)\) mein farq na karna: \(f'(x)\) ek function hai jo har \(x\) par gradient deta hai; \(f'(a)\) sirf ek number hai, ek point ka gradient.
4. Newton ka dot harf ke saath power ki tarah likh dena (jaise kitab mein chhapa hai). Dot harf ke oopar aata hai: \(\dot{y}\).
